newsitem.title: USA: N.H. Supreme Court kicks tax suit to lower court.
newsitem.headline: N.H. Supreme Court kicks tax suit to lower court.

text.p: The New Hampshire Supreme Court Thursday remanded a $100 million legal challenge of the state's interest and dividends tax back to a superior court for resolution.

The five percent tax is currently levied on bank interest and stock dividends over $2,400 paid to New Hampshire residents. Until two years ago, the state was only levying the tax on state residents who deposited their funds in out of state banks.
After legal challenges were filed contesting taxes collected from 1991 to 1993, the state admitted the policy violated the federal interstate commerce clause and abandoned the practice.
But attorneys for more than 10,000 people continued to pursue a class action lawsuit seeking $100 million in refunds.
The state has indicated it may have to pay an estimated $3 million if it paid refunds.
The high court ruling found that the interest and dividends tax complies with the state constitution, but it also violated the U.S. Constitution.
The court said the state could consider refunds only "upon the victims of its discrimination" or tax the interest and dividends of New Hampshire residents who were not taxed.
A court date for the case has not been set.
